presets.descriptionEn: A single item · pickup or van

classes.capacityCopyHe: מתאים לכמה פריטים גדולים — מקרר, מכונת כביסה, ספה או ערימת קרטונים. המשטח פתוח, אז ביום גשום עדיף לבחור רכב סגור.
classes.capacityCopyEn: A handful of large items — a fridge, a washing machine, a sofa or a pile of boxes. The bed is open, so on a rainy day choose a closed vehicle.

classes.capacityCopyHe: מתאים לחדר אחד — מיטת יחיד, שידה ו-10 עד 15 קרטונים. מספיק קטנה כדי להיכנס לחניון תת־קרקעי ולרחובות צרים בעיר.
classes.capacityCopyEn: Right for one room — a single bed, a dresser and 10–15 boxes. Small enough for underground car parks and narrow city streets.

classes.capacityCopyHe: מתאים ליחידת דיור או לדירת 2 חדרים עם ריהוט בסיסי — מיטה, ספה, שולחן וכ-20 קרטונים. סגורה לגמרי, הרהיטים מוגנים מגשם ומאבק.
classes.capacityCopyEn: Fits a studio or a small one-bedroom with basic furniture — bed, sofa, table and around 20 boxes. Fully enclosed, so nothing gets rained on.

classes.capacityCopyHe: מתאים לדירת 2–3 חדרים — סלון, חדר שינה, מטבח וכל הקרטונים. זו המשאית הכי נפוצה להובלת דירה שלמה, אבל היא לא נכנסת לחניון תת־קרקעי.
classes.capacityCopyEn: Fits a 2–3 room apartment — living room, bedroom, kitchen and every box. The standard truck for a whole-apartment move, but it cannot enter an underground car park.

classes.capacityCopyHe: מתאים לדירת 4–5 חדרים או לבית פרטי — הכול עולה בנסיעה אחת, בלי לחזור פעמיים. צריכה חניה רחבה ברחוב, לא נכנסת לחניון תת־קרקעי.
classes.capacityCopyEn: Fits a 4–5 room apartment or a private house — everything in one trip, no second run. Needs wide street parking; it will not enter an underground car park.

classes.capacityCopyHe: בשביל מה שלא עובר בחדר מדרגות — הארון והספה יוצאים דרך המרפסת. המשאית לוקחת גם את שאר תכולת הדירה באותה נסיעה.
classes.capacityCopyEn: For when the wardrobe or the sofa will not go down the stairwell — they go out through the balcony instead. It carries the rest of the flat in the same trip.

vehicles.notes:
REFERENCE VEHICLES PER CLASS

pickup (טנדר) — Toyota Hilux double cab, Mitsubishi L200, Isuzu D-Max. Modelled on the double-cab, which is the modal טנדר on Israeli roads: deck 152x152x48cm, GVW ~2.9-3.2t, legal payload ~1,000kg (I set 800kg as the working figure — drivers rarely load to plate). Volume 2.5 m³ assumes a strapped load stacked above the bed sides; a level load is only ~1.1 m³. Single-cab and flatbed conversions exist with a ~230cm deck and ~1,000kg payload; modelling the smaller double cab under-promises on purpose. Confidence high (published OEM specs, homogeneous fleet).

small_van (מסחרית קטנה) — Citroën Berlingo / Peugeot Partner / Renault Kangoo Maxi / VW Caddy, L1 body. 3.3 m³, 180x162x125cm (162 is max width; only ~123cm between the wheel arches — a 160cm-wide wardrobe will not lie flat). Payload 650kg. Confidence high.

van (מסחרית סגורה) — Mercedes Sprinter L2H2, Ford Transit L3H2, Renault Master L2H2. This class spans 9.5-11.5 m³ nominal across those three; 10 m³ is the honest middle. Raw box multiplies to ~10.6 m³, so 10 is the usable figure net of wheel arches. Payload 1,200kg is what remains under a 3.5t GVW plate after body and crew. Confidence high.

box_truck_4t (משאית 4 טון) — Isuzu NQR 75 / NPR, Mitsubishi Fuso Canter 7C18. "4 טון" in Israel names the payload, not the plate: these are ~7.5t GVW chassis with ~3.3-4t left after an Israeli-built box (מרכב). Body dims are the soft number — boxes are built locally to order, so 5.0-6.2m length and 2.1-2.3m height are all common. Confidence medium for that reason; payload and licence are solid.

box_truck_8t (משאית 8 טון) — Isuzu FVR / Forward, Fuso Fighter/FK, ~15t GVW class. 38 m³ usable out of a ~41 m³ raw box (720x240x240). Same caveat: local bodybuilders, so ±4 m³ across real fleet. Confidence medium.

crane_truck (משאית עם מנוף) — a 4t-class chassis (Isuzu NQR / Fuso Canter) with a knuckle-boom loader crane (Hiab / Fassi / Palfinger, ~3-5 t·m) mounted behind the cab. Modelled as crane + closed box on one vehicle, because dispatching a hoist and a haul separately doubles the cost. The crane and its subframe cost roughly 1,200-1,600kg of payload and ~1.2m of deck, which is why this class carries less than a plain 4-tonner despite the same chassis. Confidence low: crane make, reach and capacity vary enormously across the real fleet, and some operators run an open flatbed rather than a box — expect to correct these from real driver registrations. The per-vehicle `hasCrane` / `hasTailLift` overrides on VehicleSchema are the right place for that variance.

THE 200cm UNDERGROUND CAR PARK GATE

Only pickup (185cm) and small_van (183cm) clear a 200cm barrier, and both with under 20cm of margin. Two caveats worth encoding rather than trusting:
- A pickup carrying anything stacked above the cab is over 200cm even though the vehicle spec says 185. The gate should be evaluated against load height, not just class height, for pickup.
- Roof bars, aftermarket AC pods and roof racks push real small vans over 190cm. Consider a per-vehicle height override on VehicleSchema (there is currently none) rather than relying on the class default, and treat a 200cm cap as ~190cm effective for eligibility.
Every truck class (340-380cm) is out by a wide margin, which is the point: this field is what stops dispatching a 4-tonner to a Tel Aviv building whose only access is the ramp.

ISRAELI LICENCE CATEGORIES

B — up to 3,500kg GVW. Covers pickup, small_van and van. Note that the van class sits right on the 3.5t line: a Sprinter 519 or a Master 3.5t+ variant is C1 territory, so validate against the actual רישיון רכב GVW at driver onboarding rather than inferring from class.
C1 — 3,500-12,000kg. Covers box_truck_4t (~7.5t GVW) and crane_truck. Minimum age 21, requires the professional medical (בדיקות רפואיות) and periodic renewal.
C — above 12,000kg. Required for box_truck_8t (~15t GVW). Some trucks sold as "8 טון" are plated at exactly 12t; if a driver registers one, it is C1 not C. Again: read the GVW off the vehicle registration, do not trust the class default.

Separate from the driving licence: operating a truck-mounted loader crane over 1 tonne requires a Ministry of Labour crane operator permit (הסמכת מפעיל מנוף). That is not a licence category — it belongs in Driver.capabilities, and crane_truck jobs should require it there. Recommend adding it as a well-known capability key rather than a free-string.

OTHER THINGS WORTH KNOWING

- minCrew reflects what the job actually needs, not what the vehicle needs: crane_truck is 3 because someone operates the crane, someone receives on the balcony and someone works the apartment. box_truck_8t is 3 for the same reason (volume, not weight, drives crew).
- Volumes are calibrated against Israeli apartment conventions (rooms counted including the living room, per the comment in catalog.ts): ~3-5 m³ per room of contents, so 3 חדרים ≈ 20-24 m³ → box_truck_4t, 5 חדרים ≈ 35-40 m³ → box_truck_8t. The 1.25 headroom default in recommendVehicleClass sits on top of these, which is the right place for it.
- The van→box_truck_4t step is the largest jump in the ladder (10 → 22 m³). Anything between 12 and 17 m³ gets over-trucked to a 4-tonner. If Phase 0 data shows a cluster there, a Sprinter L4H3 / Master L3H3 "מסחרית ארוכה" at ~15-17 m³ is the missing rung — and it is still licence B and still fits streets a truck cannot.
- box_truck_4t and box_truck_8t both hit municipal weight and access restrictions in central Tel Aviv, the Jerusalem old neighbourhoods and parts of Haifa. Worth a future access constraint on the job side.
- vehicle.ts currently documents the van class as "מסחרית" in the VehicleClassId JSDoc; the seed data here uses "מסחרית סגורה" as specified. Recommend aligning the comment at D:\Claude Code\HAUL\packages\types\src\vehicle.ts line 21.

market.findings:
## Summary

Israeli movers almost never sell the way a rate card models the world. They quote a **whole-job lump sum** based on a phone/WhatsApp survey (rooms, floors, elevator, crane y/n), not base-fare + per-km + per-hour. So the two things I could source *directly and well* are (a) whole-apartment totals and (b) crane rates. The decomposed unit rates (base fare by vehicle, per-km, per-mover-hour, long carry) are **reconstructed** so they roughly reproduce the sourced totals. Treat them as a starting scaffold that recalibration should move hardest.

## VAT

Israel VAT = **18%** (raised 17%→18% Jan 2025; the proposed rise to 19% for Jan 2026 was dropped, rate held at 18%). Every number in the rate card below is **VAT-inclusive consumer shekels**. Where a source quoted ex-VAT I converted at ×1.18 and say so. Notably: `midrag.co.il/Content/Price/8708` and the `hamanof.net` crane operator list are explicitly **ex-VAT**; `pro.co.il`, `midrag` Tel Aviv page, and `toviloti` are explicitly **incl-VAT**. Most mover-owned sites state nothing at all — Israeli consumer marketing convention is that a headline shekel price to a private customer is VAT-inclusive, so I read the silent ones as incl-VAT.

## Whole-apartment totals — the strongest data

Source spread for a standard local move (elevator or ground floor, no crane, no packing), VAT-incl:

| Source | 2 rm | 3 rm | 4 rm | 5 rm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pro.co.il (marketplace, aggregated real quotes, incl-VAT) | 1,700–2,300 (avg 2,000) | 2,600–3,300 (avg 2,950) | 3,400–4,500 (avg 3,950) | 4,500–6,500 (avg 5,500) |
| midrag Tel Aviv (marketplace, incl-VAT, seasonal) | 1,379–1,618 (summer, w/ disassembly) | 2,018–2,369 (basic) | 2,597–3,049 (summer, no packing) | 3,161–3,710 (basic) |
| hvl.co.il | 1,100–1,600 | 1,950–2,950 | 2,300–3,400 | 3,150–4,450 |
| movers.org.il | 800–2,000 | 1,500–2,800 | 2,000–3,500 | 3,500–4,500 |
| moving-israel.co.il | 1,000–1,800 | 1,500–2,500 | 1,800–3,500 | 2,000–4,500 |
| toviloti.co.il (incl-VAT, high outlier) | 2,000–2,900 | 2,700–3,800 | 3,600–5,000 | 4,600–6,400 |
| moving-center.co.il (low outlier / lead bait) | 520–1,100 | 800–1,300 | 1,290–2,100 | 1,850–3,400 |

**I weighted pro.co.il and midrag heaviest** — they are comparison marketplaces aggregating actual quotes, both explicitly state VAT-inclusive, and they bracket each other. I discarded moving-center (headline prices that no crew actually shows up for) and discounted toviloti (a lead-gen guide priced generously). Seed values land between midrag-TLV-basic and pro.co.il-average, with a modest Gush Dan uplift since Tel Aviv is the most expensive market in the country (a corroborating source puts a 3–4 room TLV move at 2,500–4,000).

## Crane (מנוף) — the critical item

**There are two different machines and they price very differently. This is the single most important structural finding.**

1. **Furniture lift / small telescopic-arm crane** (מנוף הרמה — the everyday one for apartment moves, hoisting through a window or balcony). **~350–550 ₪/hr VAT-incl.** This is what ~95% of residential moves use.
2. **Articulated arm crane truck** (מנוף זרוע / hiab — heavy or very high work). **Much dearer, with a hard 2-hour minimum.** A real operator's list (hamanof.net, explicitly ex-VAT): small arm crane 400–550/hr, medium 750–1,200/hr, large 2,500–3,000/hr, all **minimum 2 hours**; truck-with-crane for up to 8 hrs 2,750–3,500 ex-VAT. Add 18%.

**Structure is hourly, floor-banded, with a de-facto ~1hr minimum call-out** (2hr for arm cranes):

- pro.co.il: 350–500/hr, avg **425**, incl-VAT
- midrag (Content/Price/16147): 400–500/hr incl-VAT, **+50 ₪/hr per floor above the 7th**
- midrag (Content/Price/8708), **ex-VAT**: floors 1–6 → 400–500/hr; floors 6–10 → 400–800/hr; floors 10+ → **1,000–1,500/hr**; +50–100 ₪ per floor above 10. Partial hours **prorated**, not rounded up. (×1.18 → ~472–590, ~472–944, ~1,180–1,770 incl-VAT.)
- hvl.co.il: small crane (≤6 floors) 400–600/hr; medium (≤10) 500–900/hr; large (≤15) 1,000–1,500/hr
- getmoving: ~400/hr; aviv-moving: 300–400/hr, rising 50–100 ₪ per floor

The most useful evidence is **aviv-moving's table of real job prices**, which reveals the effective minimum:
- Dining set to 4th floor, 30 min → **300–350** (i.e. a half-hour job still costs ~a full call-out)
- Piano to 6th floor → 400–450
- Bedroom suite from 6th floor → 400–450
- Multiple items from 8th floor → 550–600
- **Two hours of furniture to 5th floor → 800–850**

So: **call-out ≈ 500 covers roughly the first hour at floors 1–6**, then ~450–500/hr, with floor bands escalating steeply above 7 and brutally above 10. Typical **crane line on a normal Gush Dan apartment move: 800–1,300 total** (1–2 hrs), consistent with toviloti's 800–2,000 range. Duration rule of thumb: ~1 hr for a 1–3 room flat, 1.5–2 hrs for 4–6 rooms.

## Per-floor / no-elevator — wide and inconsistent

Two competing conventions, and sources disagree badly:
- **Flat per floor:** 200–350 (moving-israel guide); 100–300 (another); **50** (getmoving, but that's for *small* single-item moves)
- **Percentage of base per floor:** +10–15%, +11–12%, +25–35%, +30–40%, +10–30% — depending on source

On a 3-room base of ~2,800, a 10–12%/floor convention yields ~280–340/floor, which reconciles with the 200–350 flat figure. I seeded **200 ₪/flight** as a middle value. **This is a genuinely wide band (100–350) and a prime recalibration target.** Also worth encoding: buildings on pillars (בניין על עמודים) effectively add a floor, and items that don't fit the elevator get carried regardless of elevator presence.

## Distance / per-km — conflicting bases, low confidence

- "3–5 ₪ per km **in addition to actual work hours**"
- "Each additional 50 km adds 400–600 ₪" → 8–12 ₪/km (but this absorbs driver time and the return leg)
- Base quotes typically **include the first ~30 km** (some say 40–49 km); TLV→Eilat (347 km) adds 900–1,300 over base
- Intercity 20–100 km moves: 1,200–2,500 all-in

Since this rate card bills labor separately, the correct analog is the **3–5 ₪/km** figure, not the 8–12. I seeded **5 ₪/km, applying only beyond a ~30 km included radius**. Within Gush Dan almost every move is inside that radius, so per-km will rarely fire — which also means it will be slow to recalibrate from local job data.

## Labor per hour per mover — derived, weak

No source publishes a clean per-mover hourly rate. What exists:
- "Additional worker **200 ₪**"; "additional hours **150 ₪/hr**"
- "Hourly labor 250–450/hr" — but that's **team + truck**, not per mover
- Vehicle-hour rates that bundle 1–2 movers: small truck (≤1.5t) 300–500/hr; 1.5–3.5t 400–650/hr; 3.5–7.5t 500–800/hr

I seeded **160 ₪/hr per mover**. Crew sizes from sources: 2–3 movers for a 3-room, scaling to 4 for 5-room.

## Base fare by vehicle — derived, weakest structural item

Israeli movers **do not publish base fare by vehicle type**; they publish job prices. I built these from the vehicle-hour rates above plus the observed job-minimum floor (single-item moves run 250–650, avg **525** per pro.co.il; many sites advertise "from 250–300 ₪"). I then checked the scaffold reproduces the sourced totals:

- 2 rm: 700 + (2 movers × 3 hr × 160) = **1,660** vs sourced ~1,900 ✓
- 3 rm: 1,000 + (3 × 4 × 160) = **2,920** vs sourced ~2,800 ✓
- 4 rm: 1,000 + (3 × 5 × 160) = **3,400** vs sourced ~3,800 ✓
- 5 rm: 1,500 + (4 × 6 × 160) = **5,340** vs sourced ~5,000 ✓

Internally coherent, but the split between base and labor is an assumption, not an observation.

## Long carry — NO SOURCE FOUND. Lowest confidence in the card.

I searched specifically for this and **found no Israeli mover publishing a per-meter or per-10m long-carry rate.** Distant parking, narrow streets, and long walks from truck to entrance are universally cited as cost drivers — the 2019 ynet consumer piece lists them among the top "landmines" (מוקשים) that produce moving-day surprises — but they are **absorbed into billed work time**, not itemized. In practice movers add a lump 100–300 ₪ for far parking, or just quote more hours. My **40 ₪ per 10 m** is a pure derivation from crew-hour cost, not a sourced figure. Treat as a placeholder; do not defend it to a customer.

Related Gush Dan cost I could not price: reserving a truck bay in Tel Aviv typically needs municipal coordination / temporary signage. I found the municipality's parking-permit pages but **no published fee for a moving-day bay reservation**, so I have not put a number on it. Worth a phone call to the עירייה rather than a guess.

## Heavy items

- **Upright piano:** pro.co.il 1,000–1,200 (avg 1,100) as a standalone job; ynet 800–1,200; movers.org.il 800–1,000; hvl ~750 avg. **Grand piano ~30% more**, 1,000–1,500.
- **Safe:** small (≤20 kg) 250–300; large (~150 kg) 650–800.
- **Anything >200 kg** (piano, safe, wall unit): 700–1,500.
- **Pool/billiard table:** 200–800.
- Jacuzzi and gym equipment are named as crane-requiring items but **no source gave a price** — my numbers there are guesses and flagged low.

**Important:** I converted these to **surcharges on top of a move**, not standalone job prices (a standalone piano job carries its own truck and call-out; a piano inside a 4-room move does not). Standalone piano job ≈ 1,100; piano as an add-on ≈ 700. Ordinary fridges/washing machines are **not** surchargeable — they're normal contents; they only appear as prices in single-item-move lists.

## Other pricing behavior worth encoding

- **Strong seasonality.** midrag's Tel Aviv data shows winter (January) quotes running **~25–30% below summer** for the same flat. Summer (Jul–Aug) and holidays carry **+20–40%**; Fridays, holiday eves, and late evenings **+25–50%**. This is a bigger swing than most of the unit rates and probably deserves a multiplier in the model.
- **Packing** is separate and commonly forgotten: 25–50 ₪/box (pro.co.il 35–45), fragile +~20%, or 1,000–1,500 for a whole flat. Boxes themselves 250–350 per 50.
- **Disassembly/reassembly** separate: 600–1,000 for a flat; a 4-door wardrobe 300–400, +50–100 per extra door.
- **Insurance** sometimes quoted at ~5% of declared value.
- The 2019 ynet piece is **7 years stale** (and predates the 17%→18% VAT change). I used it **only for surcharge structure**, not price levels — its numbers (3–4 rooms at 1,700–2,500) sit visibly below today's market.

## Confidence: MEDIUM overall

- **High:** apartment totals; crane hourly rates and floor-banded structure; VAT rate.
- **Medium:** per-floor surcharge (wide 100–350 band); piano/safe surcharges; seasonality.
- **Low:** base fare by vehicle (derived); labor per mover-hour (derived); per-km (conflicting bases, rarely fires in Gush Dan).
- **Very low / placeholder:** long carry per 10 m (**no source exists** — invented from crew-cost arithmetic); jacuzzi and gym-equipment surcharges.

Everything is VAT-inclusive at 18%. Recalibrate long carry, per-floor, and the base/labor split first — they carry the most invented content.

suggestedRateCard.craneNotes: Crane (מנוף) is standard practice in Israel, not an exception - most Gush Dan moves above the 2nd floor use one. TWO DIFFERENT MACHINES: (1) Furniture lift / small telescopic crane (מנוף הרמה) - the everyday one, hoists through window or balcony, ~350-550 ILS/hr incl VAT. This covers ~95% of residential moves. (2) Articulated arm crane truck (מנוף זרוע / hiab) - for very heavy or very high work, 900-1,800 ILS/hr incl VAT with a HARD 2-HOUR MINIMUM. STRUCTURE: hourly, floor-banded, with a de-facto ~1hr minimum call-out (2hr for arm cranes). The craneBaseShekels value of 500 is the call-out, which covers roughly the first hour at floors 1-6; bill ~450-500/hr thereafter. Partial hours are prorated, not rounded up. FLOOR BANDS (converted to VAT-incl at 18%): floors 1-6 ~470-590/hr; floors 6-10 ~470-950/hr; floors 10+ ~1,180-1,770/hr. Add ~50 ILS/hr per floor above the 7th; above the 10th add ~50-100 ILS per floor. DURATION: ~1 hr for a 2-3 room flat, 1.5-2 hrs for a 4-5 room flat. TYPICAL TOTAL CRANE LINE ON A REAL MOVE: 800-1,300 ILS incl VAT, up to 2,000 for high floors or heavy items. Real quoted jobs for calibration: dining set to 4th floor 30 min = 300-350; piano to 6th floor = 400-450; bedroom suite from 6th floor = 400-450; multiple items from 8th floor = 550-600; two hours of furniture to 5th floor = 800-850. GOTCHA: a building on pillars (בניין על עמודים) effectively adds one floor to the band.

Full table: 1rm 1,300-1,600; 2rm 1,700-2,300 (avg 2,000); 3rm 2,600-3,300 (avg 2,950); 4rm 3,400-4,500 (avg 3,950); 5rm 4,500-6,500 (avg 5,500); crane 350-500/hr (avg 425); piano 1,000-1,200; packing 35-45/box. HIGHEST WEIGHT SOURCE.

https://www.midrag.co.il/content/Price/5760 — midrag Tel Aviv-specific pricing, explicitly VAT-inclusive, and the only source showing seasonality: 3rm basic 2,018-2,369, winter w/ full services 2,381-2,795; 4rm no packing summer 2,597-3,049 vs winter 1,942-2,280 (~25-30% winter discount); 5rm basic 3,161-3,710. HIGHEST WEIGHT SOURCE for Gush Dan.

https://www.midrag.co.il/Content/Price/8708 — crane rates by floor band, explicitly EX-VAT: floors 1-6 400-500/hr; floors 6-10 400-800/hr; floors 10+ 1,000-1,500/hr; +50-100 per floor above 10; partial hours prorated. Primary source for crane floor-band structure.

https://hamanof.net/מחירון-עבודות-מנוף/ — REAL CRANE OPERATOR price list (not a lead-gen page), explicitly EX-VAT: small arm crane 400-550/hr, medium 750-1,200/hr, large 2,500-3,000/hr, ALL with 2-hour minimum; truck-with-crane up to 8 hrs 2,750-3,500. Key source for the arm-crane vs furniture-lift distinction.

https://www.aviv-moving.co.il/מנוף-הרמה/ — crane 300-400/hr rising 50-100 per floor, plus a table of REAL QUOTED JOBS that reveals the effective minimum: 30-min job to 4th floor still costs 300-350; 2 hrs to 5th floor 800-850; piano to 6th 400-450; items from 8th floor 550-600. Best evidence for call-out behavior.

https://www.hvl.co.il/מחירון-הובלות — 2rm 1,100-1,600; 3rm 1,950-2,950; 4rm 2,300-3,400; 5rm 3,150-4,450; base covers up to 30km; no-elevator +25-35%; crane small (<=6 fl) 400-600/hr, medium (<=10 fl) 500-900/hr, large (<=15 fl) 1,000-1,500/hr; piano 500-2,000; small safe 250-300, large safe (150kg) 650-800.

https://www.movers.org.il/מחירון-הובלות/ — 2rm 800-2,000; 3rm 1,500-2,800; 4rm 2,000-3,500; 5rm 3,500-4,500; piano 800-1,000; safe 200-600; pool table 200-800; no-elevator +10-30%; crane from 200-600.
https://www.moving-israel.co.il/מחירון — 2rm 1,000-1,800; 3rm 1,500-2,500; 4rm 1,800-3,500; 5rm 2,000-4,500; piano from 800; no-elevator +10-15%; job floor 250 ILS/item.

https://www.toviloti.co.il/articles/moving-cost-guide-2026 — explicitly VAT-inclusive but a HIGH OUTLIER (lead-gen guide): 2rm 2,000-2,900; 3rm 2,700-3,800; 4rm 3,600-5,000; 5rm 4,600-6,400; crane 800-2,000 total; +50km adds 400-600; no-elevator +30-40%/floor; hourly 250-450 (team+truck). Discounted in the blend.

https://www.moving-center.co.il/מחירון-הובלות/ — LOW OUTLIER, excluded from blend: 2rm 520-1,100; 3rm 800-1,300; 4rm 1,290-2,100; 5rm 1,850-3,400. Useful only for its no-elevator convention (+11-12% per floor).

audit.verdict: Not shippable as a pricing source of truth. This is a naive union of two independently-authored lists — one room-prefixed (living_*, bedroom_*), one flat (armchair, bookcase, nightstand) — merged without reconciliation. Consequences, in order of damage: (1) 4 of the 15 preset ids (27%) — bed_double, bookshelf, dining_table_6, office_desk — do not resolve against the catalog at all, so a quarter of the default inventory silently vanishes from every preset quote; the naming conventions themselves conflict (presets use bed_double / dining_table_6, catalog uses bed_double_frame / dining_table_6_seat). (2) At least 8 physical objects exist twice under different ids with DIVERGENT numbers (coffee table 4 vs 6 min, vitrine 1.1 vs 1.4 m³, shoe cabinet 0.35 vs 0.45 m³, wardrobe box 0.35 vs 0.36) — identical goods price differently depending on which button the user taps, which is a defensibility problem the moment a customer compares two quotes; bedroom_safe/safe_home is a byte-identical copy. (3) craneCandidate is not derived from any threshold — it was hand-set per item, producing a 42 kg mattress that needs a crane and an 80 kg two-door fridge that does not. Crane is the single largest line item on an Israeli move; this flag being noise is the most expensive defect here. Recommend deriving it from a rule (e.g. volume ≥ 0.8 m³ OR weight ≥ 70 kg AND non-disassemblable) rather than per-row judgement. (4) The volume/weight/minute triples are otherwise well calibrated against the anchors — density sits at 40–60 kg/m³ for furniture and 90–120 for appliances/boxes, handling at 3–5 kg/min for furniture and 8 for boxes — so the numeric scale is sound; it is the relational consistency, the boolean flags and the coverage that fail. (5) Coverage is Israel-blind in places: no stroller, no fan, no plata, no sukkah, no מיטה וחצי, no ארון שירות, and no catch-all 'other' row — while carrying a sewing machine, a surfboard and a conference table. Also flag for legal review: gas_balloon (בלון גז) is modelled as a routine 5-minute carry, but LPG cylinders are dangerous goods most movers and their insurers will not transport. Minor: bed_sofa_single_with_trundle is a bed with 'sofa' in its id.
